>
> Hi.
>
> I ran the PCR fragment length normalization. It gave me 38 warnings, all
> involving NaNs being produced

> "Is it normal to receive these warnings."

Yes, that is alright. These warnings are because the allelic
crosstalk in the first place introduces a tiny set of non-positive
values (typically for the homozygote SNPs and expected), and although
summarization makes this set even smaller, some do end up as
non-positive chip-effect estimates. Now, since the fragment-length
normalization is done on the log-scale, the negative ones obviously
become NaN:s (and the zero ones -Inf).

In general, warnings are just to make you aware of a condition (like
"FYI"). Errors are always errors and should never be ignored.

/Henrik
